threads.body: [General] This newly scoped App token does not request `workflows: write`, but the same step merges `origin/main` before pushing. When a workflow file changed after checkout, that merge makes the generated branch contain a workflow change—the case called out in the following comment—and GitHub rejects the push without workflow permission, so updates to the existing PR can still fail. Add `permission-workflows: write` to this token (as the backport workflow does) or avoid including workflow changes in this push.

replies.body:
Addressed in 07b907af3e2206a3cc003803c4280a006dbae467.

Analysis: The generated branch merges current main before the App token pushes it. That merge can include workflow changes, and GitHub requires workflow write permission for the push.

Upsides: The automation can update an existing pull request after main changes a workflow file.

Downsides: The App token receives workflow write permission for this job.
